title: Tensor Product Dehn Invariant in ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ)

problemStatement.plain: Formalize the proper tensor product Dehn invariant D(P) ∈ ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ) in Lean 4 and prove that the cube and regular tetrahedron have distinct invariants.
whyMatters: Places Hilbert's Third Problem in its correct algebraic setting (tensor product theory)
Proves the one_tmul_ne_zero lemma showing faithfully flat extension ℚ → ℝ preserves nonzero-ness
Completes the WIP open question from dissection-of-cubes-oq-02

insights: Using ℚ-tensor product (ℝ ⊗_ℚ) instead of ℤ-tensor product gives access to vector space theory: all ℚ-modules are free, so separating functionals always exist
The key proof step one_tmul_ne_zero uses Module.Free.chooseBasis to extract a basis coordinate functional — this is the constructive form of the axiom of choice in Lean
Cube angle π/2 = (1/2)π is rational multiple of π → [π/2] = 0 in ℝ/πℚ → D(cube) = 0
Tetrahedron angle arccos(1/3)/π is irrational (Niven) → [arccos(1/3)] ≠ 0 in ℝ/πℚ → D(tet) ≠ 0
smul_ne_zero pattern: n ⊗ m ≠ 0 iff n ≠ 0 (as rational) AND m ≠ 0 — requires both numeric nonzero (norm_num) and tensor nonzero (one_tmul_ne_zero)
nextSteps: Formalize variable edge length weights ℓ(e) ⊗ [θ(e)] for the full Dehn invariant
Prove Dehn's theorem directly: scissors congruence → equal Dehn invariant
Formalize Dehn-Sydler completeness: volume + Dehn invariant are complete invariants
